Sorry, wrong button. I was saying...

See ?at:

> at generates arrivals at specific absolute times.

So you are generating just one arrival per trajectory. Instead, you should use:

function() rweibull(1,sim_input[ i ,2],sim_input[ i ,3])

parts:
Inaki,

Thank you for the response.

I did something a bit different and got it to work. 

My final two questions for now, is the output from my temp%>%run(until=sim_time)  statement lists each subsystem failure with a value attached to each subsystem in ascending order. For example, the first "brakes failure" reads as brakes0 and the second reads as brakes1, so on and so forth. 


1) Is there a function within simmer to group all failures for each subsystem to analyze things such as: Average activity time, crew delay time, etc? 

2) The simulation below is for one 20 year simulation. If I want to replicate this say, 2000 times, do you have a recommendation to do this efficiently. I tried rollback, but I suspect I am placing it in the wrong place. 

Thanks so much for you input. Simmer is a great tool!

The working output is below the code for a single simulation

**Repairable Systems Simulation Tool: Subsystem Level**
=======================================================

```{r}
repair_sim_subs <- function(xxx,temp,sss,sim_time){
  
library(simmer)      ##Call Simmer Library
library(simmer.plot) ##Call Simmer Plot Library
library(gdata)       ##Call gdata Library
library(poisson)     ##Call poisson Library
library(parallel)
library(hms)
set.seed(sss)        #Set a random seed for this simulation

require(gdata)

i<- 1
sim_input <-read.xls ((xxx), sheet = 1, header = TRUE) #Read in Repairable System Spreadsheet

while(i < length(sim_input$subsystem)+1){
rep1   <- sim_input[i,4]       ##Repair distribution parameter 1
rep2   <- sim_input[i,5]       ##Repair distribution parameter 2
delay1 <- sim_input[i,15]      ##Delay distribution parameter 1
delay2 <- sim_input[i,16]      ##Delay distribution parameter 2


temp <- simmer()               ##Instantiate the environment

assign(paste0(sim_input[i,1]),           ##Unique Trajectories for each Subsystem
sub_traj <-
  trajectory(name="Subsystem's Path")%>%
log_("Subsystem has failed.")%>%
timeout(function(){runif(1,delay1,delay2)})%>%
log_("Crew Arrives.")%>%

set_attribute("Fail_time",function(){now(temp)})%>%
  seize("counter")%>%
  log_(function() {paste("Begin Repair")})%>%
  timeout(function(){runif(1,rep1,rep2)})%>%
  release("counter")%>%
  log_(function(){paste("Repaired")}),sub_traj,.GlobalEnv)
i<-i+1
}



sim_input <- assign("sim_input",sim_input,.GlobalEnv)     ##Call Excel Sheet into Trajectories

 temp <-simmer("System")%>% add_resource("counter",preemptive = TRUE)       ##Design the system

 
 for(i in 1:length(sim_input$subsystem)){
   
   ##
intensity <- function(t) (sim_input[ i ,3]/sim_input[ i ,2])*((t/sim_input[ i ,2])^sim_input[ i ,3]-1)
rate <- rweibull(sim_input[ i ,2],sim_input[ i ,3])
num.events <- 1000
keep<-nhpp.sim(rate, num.events, prob.func=intensity)

   if(length(keep[which((keep<sim_time)&(keep>0))])<1){
  
  print(paste("No",sim_input[i,1], "Failures"))
}
   
else{
  temp <- temp %>% add_generator(as.character(sim_input[ i ,1]),get(as.character(sim_input[ i ,1])),at(keep[which((keep<sim_time)&(keep>0))]))}
  
 }
 
  temp%>%run(until=1000)                              ##Run the System

  print(temp%>%                                       ##Summary Statistics for the System
  get_mon_arrivals)

plot(sub_traj)
}

#######
repair_sim_subs("simmerinput.xls",temp,sample(1:1000000,1),20)
#######

```

> temp%>%run(until=sim_time) statement lists each subsystem failure with a
> value attached to each subsystem in ascending order. For example, the first
> "brakes failure" reads as brakes0 and the second reads as brakes1, so on and
> so forth.
>
>
> 1) Is there a function within simmer to group all failures for each
> subsystem to analyze things such as: Average activity time, crew delay time,
> etc?

The log_() function is meant for debugging purposes. Once you are
satisfied with the simulation model, you should comment out all those
lines. simmer automatically monitors and records every change in the
system during simulation time. Then, there are three functions to
retrieve all this information:

get_mon_arrivals(per_resource=TRUE) # or FALSE, depending on your needs
get_mon_resources()
get_mon_attributes()

Note that you need to define "mon=2" in your generators for the last
one to work. These data frames contain all the information required to
compute any metric you want. This processing stage is out of simmer's
scope, but there are excellent tools, in base R or using other
packages, for that purpose.

> 2) The simulation below is for one 20 year simulation. If I want to
> replicate this say, 2000 times, do you have a recommendation to do this
> efficiently. I tried rollback, but I suspect I am placing it in the wrong
> place.

There is a section in the introductory vignette addressing this specific topic:

http://r-simmer.org/articles/simmer-01-introduction.html#replication
> Thanks so much for you input. Simmer is a great tool!

Much appreciated!

Iñaki

If I understand this correctly, your generators generate failures. So
the trace I saw in your last email was about many different failures
for different parts for *one* turbine, and you want to simulate many
turbines at the same time. Then, just add more generators. Instead of

add_generator("brakes", brakes_traj, brakes_dist)
add_generator("yaw", yaw_traj, yaw_dist)

etc., you'd have

add_generator("turbine0_brakes", brakes_traj, brakes_dist)
add_generator("turbine1_brakes", brakes_traj, brakes_dist)
...
add_generator("turbine0_yaw", yaw_traj, yaw_dist)
add_generator("turbine1_yaw", yaw_traj, yaw_dist)
...

and so on and so forth. You can attach as many generators as you need
to the same trajectory.

Regards,
Iñaki
